title: Fighting COVID-19 misinformation on social media: Experimental evidence for a scalable accuracy nudge intervention
paper_type: Empirical psychology / social-media behavior experiment (two studies, preprint, Psychological Science)
engine: anomalyco/opencode (ReproAI) - DeepSeek V4 Flash via uniGPT
mode: reimplementation (data obtainable from OSF project files; independent R reimplementation of the Stata .do analyses)

analysis_pipeline.description: Both studies analyzed at the rating level via OLS with two-way cluster-robust standard errors clustered on participant (id) and headline (item_num), re-implementing the authors' Stata 'cluster2' subroutine (Cameron-Gelbach-Miller additive V = V_id + V_item - V_idXitem). DV z-scored (Study 1) or rescaled to [0,1] (Study 2). Veracity and condition contrast-coded per the .do files.
analysis_pipeline.study1_preprocessing: Ratings are stored per presentation order-block; the Condition code (1-4) selects the version column (base/.0/.1/.2) for each subject. 853 subjects x 30 ratings = 25590 obs, df2=25586.
analysis_pipeline.study2_preprocessing: Ratings in base columns; 856 rows, 255 subjects complete -> 25627 obs after dropping missing, df2=25623.
analysis_pipeline.cross_check: Cluster-robust F re-computed in both a hand-rolled two-way cluster VCV (00_lib.R) and the validated 'fixest' package; both agree (Study 1 interaction F ~43.7).

reimplementation_status.study1_headline: NOT exactly reproducible: interaction F=43.70 vs 42.24; beta -0.130 (std predictors) vs -0.126; simple-effect F accuracy 52.75 vs 42.24, sharing 7.39 vs 6.74; '32.4%' claim -> 31.4% relative. Direction/significance identical.
reimplementation_status.study2_headline: Reproduces: interaction F=17.881 vs 17.88, df2=25623 exact; simple effect d=0.050/0.143 vs 0.050/0.142; discernment ratio 2.80x vs 2.8x; Figure 3 r=0.754 vs 0.76.
reimplementation_status.table1_simple_effects: Reproduce to within rounding across all five IV panels.
